History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
31-year-old man with 2-month history of fatigue, poor sleep, low appetite, mild low mood, decreased sex drive, and exertional shortness of breath; background of hypothyroidism on thyroxine; advised to arrange in-person review and blood tests.

History:
• Main concerns: “really difficult” to get up in the morning, very low energy throughout the day, poor appetite.  
• Onset/progression: Symptoms began roughly 2 months ago, coinciding with starting a new job; persisting and impacting daily function.  
• Sleep: Difficulty sleeping overall; not waking early but trouble achieving restful sleep.  
• Concentration: Feels distracted and has difficulty focusing.  
• Mood: Slightly lower than usual; denies feeling suicidal or wanting to harm self/others.  
• Libido: Decreased sex drive over the past few months; married.  
• Sexual function: Unclear change in morning erections (patient initially said none noticed recently, later stated no change – conflict noted).  
• Exertional symptoms: Shortness of breath during sports compared with a few months ago; increased fatigue on exertion.  
• Vision: No change.  
• System review otherwise not discussed; no additional complaints volunteered.

Past Medical History:
• Hypothyroidism – on long-term thyroxine therapy (dose not documented).  
• No previous mental health diagnoses reported.  
• No other chronic illnesses disclosed.

Medications:
• Thyroxine – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Married.  
• Started a new job 2 months ago (timing coincides with symptom onset).  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drug use, and other lifestyle factors not discussed.

Family History:
• Father died by suicide 15 years ago.  
• No other significant medical or psychiatric family history reported.  
• Mother well; patient is an only child.

Physical Examination:
• Not performed during teleconsultation.

Investigations:
• None to date; clinician advised blood tests at forthcoming in-person visit.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Fatigue, low mood, concentration difficulty, poor sleep:
  • Assessment: Ongoing fatigue and low mood of 2 months’ duration; differential includes depressive disorder, thyroid dysfunction, anemia, other metabolic or endocrine causes.  
  • Plan:  
    – Book in-person GP appointment within a few days.  
    – Full physical examination at that visit.  
    – Screening blood tests (clinician stated “blood tests,” specifics not detailed).  
    – Monitor mood; patient advised to seek help promptly if suicidal thoughts emerge.

Issue 2 – Known hypothyroidism:
  • Assessment: Possible contribution to current symptoms; adequacy of replacement therapy uncertain.  
  • Plan:  
    – Include thyroid function tests with blood work.  
    – Review thyroxine dose and compliance at GP visit.

Issue 3 – Decreased libido and exertional shortness of breath:
  • Assessment: May be secondary to fatigue, mood, or endocrine issues; shortness of breath requires evaluation for cardiopulmonary or fitness changes.  
  • Plan:  
    – Discuss during in-person review; consider cardiopulmonary exam and further testing as indicated after initial work-up.

General plan items:
  • Provide reassurance that further evaluation is underway.  
  • Safety-netting: patient denies suicidality; advised to seek urgent help if this changes.

Quality checks:

Missing but expected elements:
• Vital signs, physical examination findings.  
• Detailed review of systems.  
• Smoking/alcohol/substance history.  
• Medication dose, route, and frequency.  
• Allergy confirmation for non-drug allergens.  

Internal conflicts:
• Patient first implied absence of morning erections, later stated no change – conflict noted.

Transcript quality:
• Generally clear; minor connectivity pauses; no significant inaudible sections.
